packet.title: Schematron as a front end to the XSLT AST (design)
packet.summary: Designs Schematron as a front end that reads a .sch document into the XSLT AST, which the existing XSLT lowering compiles, with findings as a public sxml_schematron_report and errors located in the .sch.

body.p: The owner accepted Schematron on 2026-10-28, as a front end beside XSLT and XQuery, not by generating XSLT text. The owner settled the open points in (edition 2025, bindings, outputs, exit status, order with XSD, SchXslt as a test reference only): the design follows them. No phase covered it (PLAN.md names XSD only): the packet's decision record brings it into Phase 7. Evidence from 2026-10-28 (see , and the queue):

item.p: the official pre-compiled EN 16931 stylesheets pass all 1,133 checks of the EN 16931 UBL unit tests on sxml;

SchXslt 1.10.1 running on sxml compiles the EN 16931 sources into a stylesheet that also passes 1,133 of 1,133, but its text pipeline costs 10.5 s for EN 16931 (8 min 56 s before perf-5 to perf-7 and without SchXslt's sort-once fix) and needs more than the default step bound: the cost is in generating XSLT text, not in Schematron;
XRechnung's rules embed XSLT (xsl:function for xr:checkIBAN), as the xslt2 and xslt3 query bindings allow;
findings today are SVRL with an XPath for a location, and errors in a rule point into the generated stylesheet, not the .sch.

Whom it serves, first: the maintainer of a rule set (errors at rules.sch:LINE:COLUMN) and the person reading a finding (the document's line and column, with the locations proposal under "## Proposed" in DECISIONS.md); then embedders (C, JavaScript) who validate many documents without bundling a third-party stylesheet. Who pays: a reader and an expansion pass in C, one public header, a CLI option, the JavaScript API, the book; nothing per event of other languages.
Design (decision record, glossary terms first, public header):

The path: the .sch document is parsed by the processor's XML parser (with locations kept); a Schematron reader builds the XSLT AST (src/xslt_ast_internal.h: sxml_xslt_ast_add_node, _add_attribute, _append_child), as src/xslt_read.c does for a stylesheet, with each node's source location in the .sch; the existing XSLT lowering makes IR. No IR kind, no evaluator change, no generated XSLT text. Lowering Schematron to IR directly is rejected: it would duplicate modes, patterns and priorities.

The mapping, each with its section of ISO/IEC 19757-3 (the packet names the edition it implements, after checking the current one): pattern to mode; rule to template rule matching its context, rule order to priority (the first matching rule of a pattern fires); let to a variable; assert and report to a condition that adds a finding; value-of, name, diagnostics, properties, role and flag; phases selecting modes; ns declarations; include, extends and abstract patterns expanded while reading, in one linear pass (each placeholder replaced once, longest name first, without a regex per parameter); documents. Foreign xsl:function, xsl:key, xsl:include and xsl:import children of sch:schema under the xslt2 and xslt3 bindings become the same AST nodes src/xslt_read.c makes; other bindings are rejected in one place with the error the standard gives, or mapped if the decision record shows they are the same language.

Findings: a public sxml_schematron_report modelled on sxml_schema_report (include/sxml/schema.h): the assert or report id, its role and flag, the message text, the rule's location in the .sch and the node's location in the document; delivered to a report sink like the XSD validator's. SVRL is one output form, made from the reports, not the engine's data.

API (include/sxml/schematron.h, new, additive; at most three parameters; the object lifecycle of CLAUDE.md): compile a Schematron schema once (with phase and parameters), validate many documents or nodes with it; typed (validated) input allowed.

CLI (docs/CLI.md, : no new command): sxml validate --schematron=FILE [--phase=NAME], combinable with --schema; text and --format=json reports as for XSD, the same exit statuses; --format=svrl if the decision record keeps it.
JavaScript: the same compile-once, validate-many shape in the package.
Out of scope: streaming validation, Schematron Quick Fix, any output other than reports and SVRL.

Owns: include/sxml/schematron.h (new), the decision record, docs/GLOSSARY.md terms, and the implementation packet 's text (its files, gates and order). The CLI design is written in the decision record: docs/CLI.md is cli-4's while 7.27 runs, and 7.28 updates its validate section.
Done when: the owner has reviewed the header and the decision record; 7.28 is written with its file list and gates.

body.p: Designed 2026-10-28 (), for the owner's review: include/sxml/schematron.h (compiles with the project's flags under clang and gcc, implemented by nothing yet), , the glossary's Schematron terms, 7.28 below. Not ticked: the owner's review is the gate.

Revised 2026-10-28 after the owner's review (, points A to D; point 2 amended: no queryBinding, xslt and xpath are read as XSLT 4.0 and XPath 4.0) and against the text of ISO/IEC 19757-3:2025: every construct of the 2025 edition designed with its clause (group, library, rules, extends at the top, schema and abstract-pattern params, let/@as, visit-each, severity, dynamic flag/role/severity, phase from/when and #ANY, schematronEdition); compile errors through a report sink; exit status 1 for an unsupported binding. The header, , the glossary and 7.28 below follow.

Done 2026-10-28 (, accepted by the owner): the owner answered the revision's eight choices (, "The owner's answers": severity decides when present; xslt4/xpath4 as 4.0; rule contexts are XSLT patterns under every binding; no text value templates; schema parameters are compile-time text; rule lets once per context node; XSLT's compiler gets a report sink in 7.28; any schematronEdition accepted and reported). The header, the glossary and 7.28 follow.
